I am a 45-year-old farmer with 15 years of experience farming these 6 mu in Quzhou. I have a household of seven to feed, so I need to get the most out of this land without taking foolish risks. I have been doing the wheat-maize double crop rotation for years, and it is what works on the North China Plain. My well gives me water when the rains do not come, but I still need to be careful with costs.

For wheat, I will plant an improved variety in autumn right after deep rotary tillage. I have learned that a well-prepared seedbed matters for winter wheat. I will apply fertilizer—mainly nitrogen, but also some phosphorus and potassium—because the soil here needs it after taking out the maize. I will irrigate four times: before winter, at green-up, at jointing, and at flowering. Those are the critical times. I will spray pesticide three times to deal with aphids and powdery mildew, which always show up.

For maize, I will plant a hybrid variety immediately after wheat harvest in early June. Timing is everything for the summer crop, so I will use no-tillage planting to save time and keep soil moisture. Maize grows fast and needs water during the big growth period and grain filling, so I will irrigate three times. I will apply nitrogen and some P and K, but not as much as wheat because maize is efficient. I will spray pesticide twice, mainly to control corn borer and armyworm. I expect good yields if the weather cooperates—wheat around 450 jin per mu is normal for me, and maize can reach 550 jin per mu with a hybrid.
